bull.b: FDA and EMA approval to combine all HLA types in randomized arms increases the eligible patient population and expands the potential commercial opportunity for GLSI-100.

Open-label results and existing trial data showed statistically significant reductions in cancer recurrence across HLA groups versus historical control, supporting a higher likelihood of meaningful treatment benefit.
A group-sequential study design and faster event accumulation enable interim analyses that could support regulatory filings if strong treatment effects are observed.

bear.b: Uncertainty about whether GLSI-100 provides comparable protection in the newly included non-HLA-A*02 patients creates a clear clinical risk to trial outcomes.
Reliance on a historical Phase 3 comparator and open-label comparisons may raise questions about comparability and complicate regulatory assessment of efficacy.
Combining multiple HLA types could increase patient heterogeneity, which may dilute the observed treatment effect and increase the risk of inconclusive interim analyses.
